newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Infra to buy China power plant.
newsitem.headline: New World Infra to buy China power plant.

text.p: New World Infrastructure Ltd said it is acquiring a controlling interest in a power plant project in China.

New World Infrastructure said in a statement published on Thursday that it would acquire a 60 percent interest in Shunde De Sheng Power Plant Co Ltd for US$51.74 million from third party Talent Classic Enterprise Ltd.
Shunde De Sheng is a Sino-foreign equity joint venture held currently 70 percent by Talent Classic and 30 percent by Shunde Electric Development Co.

Talent Classic would sell a 60 percent stake to New World Infrastructure and a 10 percent stake to Shunde Electric, following which the status of the venture will be changed to a Sino-foreign co-operative joint venture, the statement said.
New World Infrastructure said it has also agreed to provide a shareholder's loan of not more than US$101.08 million to De Sheng Power Co.

Of the purchase price, US$17.00 milllion had been advanced and the balance of US$34.74 million will be paid in cash on completion of the agreement. With the loan, the total investment of New World Infrastructure will amount to US$152.82 million,
Shunde De Sheng Power had unaudited net profit of of 131.18 million yuan in 1996 and an unaudited net asset value of 511.44 million.
New World Infrastructure shares were down HK$0.10 at HK$22.10 in early trade on Thursday.
